WHO Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Hypertension in Adults
Publication Date: August 2021 | World Health Organization (WHO)
Topic: Essential and Secondary Hypertension Management
Recommendation 1: Diagnostic Threshold for Hypertension
WHO recommends initiating pharmacological treatment of hypertension in individuals with a confirmed diagnosis
Recommendation 2: Target Blood Pressure Thresholds
WHO suggests a target blood pressure treatment goal of < 140/90 mmHg in all patients with hypertension withou
Recommendation 3: Pharmacological Monotherapy vs Dual Therapy
For adults requiring pharmacological treatment, initial monotherapy or dual combination therapy using classes fro
1. Thiazide or thiazide-like diuretics (e.g. Chlorthalidone, Hydrochlorothiazide)
2. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) or Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs, e.g. Telmisartan)
3. Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (CCBs, e.g. Amlodipine).
